# FROZEN FIXTURE - do not edit, do not 'update' to match bootstrap.sh.
#
# The five console helpers (log/ok/warn/err/t) plus the EMAIL+NAME inline
# quick-mint sub-block of bootstrap.sh exactly as they stood at commit
# ffddd85 (origin/main, 2026-09-27) -- the commit MYC-5093 branched from, and
# the last commit BEFORE the quick-mint-reused-is-a-warning fix. At that SHA,
# a resubmit for an email with an already-live token came back
# {ok:true, reused:true, resent:<bool>} with no "token" field. The inline
# mint block only recognized a 32-hex "token" field: anything else -- this
# reply included -- fell through to err("Inline mint failed. Falling back to
# form."), landing on the FAILED list and telling the end-of-run summary the
# install needs a re-run, which re-sends the welcome email every time.
#
# Extracted verbatim with `git show ffddd85:bootstrap.sh | sed -n '...'`,
# never retyped and never hand-edited, so this can't silently drift from the
# real pre-fix source (same technique as
# tests/fixtures/bootstrap-prefix-e9f80e0.sh.txt and
# tests/fixtures/bootstrap-prefix-27d5243-parent.sh.txt).
#
# Used by tests/integration/test_bootstrap_quick_mint_reused.sh as the
# NEGATIVE CONTROL "before" source: the harness built from this fixture must
# call err() and must NOT recognize a reused+resent reply, proving the test
# would have caught the bug it exists to catch.
#
# A pinned commit SHA is immutable, but a shallow CI checkout may not have it
# in its object store -- so this is a vendored file, never `git show
# ffddd85:bootstrap.sh` run live in the test itself.

# ── console helpers (log/ok/warn/err/t), verbatim from ffddd85 ──
log()  { printf "  \033[36m·\033[0m %s\n" "$*"; }
ok()   { printf "  \033[32m✓\033[0m %s\n" "$*"; }
warn() { printf "  \033[33m!\033[0m %s\n" "$*"; }
err()  { printf "  \033[31m✗\033[0m %s\n" "$*"; FAILED+=("$*"); }
t() { [[ "$LANG_CODE" == "es" ]] && echo "$2" || echo "$1"; }

# ── EMAIL+NAME inline quick-mint sub-block, verbatim from ffddd85 ──
  if [[ -z "${TOKEN:-}" && -n "${EMAIL:-}" && -n "${NAME:-}" ]]; then
    QM_LANG="${LANG_HINT:-en}"
    [[ "$QM_LANG" != "en" && "$QM_LANG" != "es" ]] && QM_LANG="en"
    QM_OS="mac-arm"
    case "$(uname -sm 2>/dev/null)" in
      Darwin*arm64*) QM_OS="mac-arm" ;;
      Darwin*x86_64*) QM_OS="mac-intel" ;;
      Linux*) QM_OS="linux" ;;
    esac
    log "$(t "Minting install token for $EMAIL via $INSTALL_API_BASE..." \
            "Generando token de instalación para $EMAIL en $INSTALL_API_BASE...")"
    QM_PAYLOAD="$(EMAIL="$EMAIL" NAME="$NAME" QM_LANG="$QM_LANG" QM_OS="$QM_OS" "$PY" <<'PY'
import json, os
print(json.dumps({
  "email": os.environ.get("EMAIL",""),
  "name": os.environ.get("NAME",""),
  "lang": os.environ.get("QM_LANG","en"),
  "os": os.environ.get("QM_OS","mac-arm"),
  "consentRequired": True,
}))
PY
)"
    set +e
    QM_RESP="$(curl -sSL -m 12 -X POST "$INSTALL_API_BASE/api/install/quick-mint" \
      -H "content-type: application/json" \
      -d "$QM_PAYLOAD" 2>/dev/null)"
    set -e
    QM_TOKEN="$(printf '%s' "${QM_RESP:-}" | "$PY" -c '
import json, sys
try:
    d = json.load(sys.stdin)
    print(d.get("token","") if d.get("ok") else "")
except Exception:
    print("")
' 2>/dev/null)"
    if [[ -z "$QM_TOKEN" || ! "$QM_TOKEN" =~ ^[a-f0-9]{32}$ ]]; then
      err "$(t "Inline mint failed. Falling back to form." \
              "Falló la generación inline. Caemos al formulario.")"
    else
      ok "$(t "Token minted inline. No browser needed." \
              "Token generado en línea. Sin navegador.")"
      TOKEN="$QM_TOKEN"
    fi
  fi
